stories.title: Do the Shetland Isles need Cold War-style military protection?
summary: Calls are being made for the defence of the Shetland Isles to be strengthened after increased sightings of Russian trawlers off the coast of Scotland.

stories.title: 'New kit' helps battle against bugs
summary: The chemical-free decoys are used while clearing riverside vegetation.

stories.title: IceCube detects ghost particles with 10 billion times the energy of solar neutrinos
summary: Mysterious particles called neutrinos constantly stream through our bodies, and scientists are now detecting incredibly powerful versions arriving from distant cosmic sources using a massive observatory buried in Antarctic ice.
These elusive “ghost particles” could hold extraordinary clues about the Big Bang, extreme cosmic events, and some of the universe’s greatest mysteries.

stories.title: Scientists discover that some “unhealthy” diets can boost cancer immunotherapy in mice
summary: In a surprising discovery, scientists found that certain diets associated with obesity can make cancer immunotherapy more effective in mice, challenging traditional assumptions about diet and cancer treatment.
The findings suggest that the secret may lie in how food interacts with gut bacteria to strengthen the immune system's response to cancer.

stories.title: NASA reveals a haunting skull hidden in Antarctica’s ice
summary: NASA satellites have captured an eerie, skull-shaped formation on a remote Antarctic island, but its haunting appearance conceals a troubling warning about melting glaciers.
Unusually warm winter temperatures have exposed large areas of dark ice, potentially accelerating future melting and gradually transforming the skull's ghostly features.

stories.title: 30,000-year-old DNA reveals Ice Age Europeans were far more connected than we thought
summary: Scientists have uncovered surprising DNA evidence that Europeans living more than 30,000 years ago were connected across vast distances, challenging the idea that ancient populations remained largely isolated.
Genetic clues from human remains and cave sediments reveal prehistoric migration, long-lasting communities, and survival through the harshest conditions of the Ice Age.

stories.title: Woman who flew with swans warns of lead danger
summary: Sacha Dench, known as the "human swan", welcomes new laws banning the sale of lead ammunition.

stories.title: Verdict delayed on controversial sea defences
summary: The council have deferred a decision on the building of 17 rock groynes after RNLI safety concerns.

stories.title: NASA's Hubble and Webb discover ancient worlds that remember their past
summary: NASA’s Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes have uncovered surprising clues about the solar system’s origins by studying 27 tiny, distant objects beyond Neptune.

Scientists discovered that these ancient building blocks of planets have remained remarkably unchanged for billions of years, while their unexpected sizes and numbers challenge existing theories of planet formation.

stories.title: 'Fascinating' rare beetle found in Wales again after 60 years
summary: It was feared The Short-Necked Oil Beetle had become extinct in Wales after recent surveys.

stories.title: Common pesticide linked to 2.5 times the risk of Parkinson’s disease
summary: A UCLA study found that long-term exposure to a common pesticide was linked to more than 2.5 times the risk of Parkinson's disease.
Scientists also uncovered how the chemical damages brain cells and identified a promising way to protect them.

stories.title: Aquarium shark that helped 'dispel myths' dies
summary: Staff at Plymouth's aquarium pay tribute to a sand tiger shark believed to be almost 30 years old.

stories.title: Scientists shrink Archimedes’ screw to the size of a single molecule
summary: Scientists have built a groundbreaking molecular motor that spins in either direction using electricity, inspired by a machine invented more than 2,000 years ago.
Even more remarkably, its rotation can boost electrical conductivity by up to 100 times, potentially transforming the future of molecular electronics.
